newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Environmental claims against Iraq hit $32 billion.
newsitem.headline: Environmental claims against Iraq hit $32 billion.

text.p: Nine countries, including Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, have filed $32 billion in claims against Iraq for environmental damage caused during the Gulf War, a U.N. spokeswoman said on Friday.

Baghdad's troops are alleged to have discharged millions of barrels of oil into the Gulf in January 1991 and ignited more than 700 oilwells in Kuwait the following month before fleeing a U.S.-led multinational liberation force.

A spokeswoman told a news briefing that states which met the February 1 deadline for filing environmental claims at the U.N. Compensation Commission were: Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the United States, Iran, Britain, Australia, Germany, the Netherlands and Turkey.
Canada also filed a request, according to U.N. sources.
The U.S. claim was nearly $8.8 million, U.S. diplomats said.
Kuwait filed a $16.3 billion claim, while Saudi Arabia and Iran, which also border the Gulf, each filed claims in the billions of dollars, they added.
Diplomats hope its Governing Body, made up of the same 15 members as the Security Council, will name arbitrators by year- end. They will assess damages and announce successful claims.

The Gulf War reparations fund, set up by Security Council in 1991 to assess damages caused by Iraq's invasion and seven-month occupation of Kuwait, has received more than $220 billion in claims from individuals, companies and governments.

Funded by governmental contributions and seized Iraqi assets, it has been perpetually cash-strapped. So far it has only paid out $13.5 million to 4,000 priority claimants proving serious personal injury or death of a close relative.

But it has been boosted by the implementation since last December of the U.N. and Iraq "oil-for-food deal", under which it is to get 30 per cent of revenues, or $100 million monthly. So far, it has received $72 million from the proceeds.
